title: Assurance of one’s justification is not the same necessity as assent to articles of faith
source_text: XXXVII. Praeterea juxta communem Protestantium doctrinam, ut clarum est ex iis quae superiori disputatione exposita fuerunt, certitudo quam quis habet de sua coram Deo justificatione non est ejusdem omnino rationis, cum certitudine illa quam habemus de fidei articulis, & dogmatibus illis quae verbo Dei expresse continentur, nempe, neque tanta est, neque paris necessitatis: cum pro infideli merito habeatur qui revocat in dubium an Jesus sit Dei filius; non vero statim quicunque dubitat an peccatorum suorum remissionem adeptus sit, quia pro certo statuere non audet suam fidem & poenitentiam satis veram & synceram esse. Adeoque hic quaestio non est, An eadem omnino fide qua fidei dogmata creduntur, teneatur quisque fidelis credere se esse in Dei gratia, seque vere regeneratum & justificatum esse; cum inter haec diversitatem quandam agnoscant Protestantes.
pass_a_gloss: Besides, according to the common doctrine of Protestants, as is clear from those things which were set out in the preceding disputation, the certainty which someone has concerning his justification before God is not of altogether the same reason as that certainty which we have concerning the articles of faith and those dogmas which are expressly contained in the Word of God—namely, it is neither so great nor of equal necessity: since he is deservedly held for an unbeliever who calls into doubt whether Jesus is the Son of God; but not immediately whoever doubts whether he has obtained remission of his sins, because he does not dare to determine as certain that his faith and repentance are sufficiently true and sincere. And so here the question is not whether by altogether the same faith by which the dogmas of faith are believed each faithful person is bound to believe that he is in God’s grace and truly regenerated and justified; since Protestants acknowledge a certain diversity between these.
pass_b_english: Doubting a gospel article unbelief; doubting one’s own sincerity need not.
Protestants refuse to equate assurance of status with assent to the creed.
